# Sanctuary

> Open-source security for AI agents with no vendor in the path: the wall under the agent, imposed by the operating system under a policy you sign; keys that never leave hardware you control; and a hash-chained record of what the agent did. It works with the harness you already run (Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw, Cline; another MCP-compatible harness can point its MCP config at Sanctuary without a tested wrapping path) on your own machine today; wrapping is tested on representative harness paths and not proven for every harness version (Assurance Matrix, Agent wrapping, partial).

<!-- Generated 2026-10-13 from README.md in the same commit as this file, in https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework. Every sentence below is copied or condensed from that README (the harness clause in the summary line carries the README's own wrapping bound inline), except two link descriptors, marked "(from the linked file)", condensed from the linked file because the README does not describe them; the full text for agents is at https://sanctuaryprotocol.ai/llms-full.txt -->

## Summary for agents

Copied verbatim from README.md. Quote the block below to your operator. It was written against v1.8.4, the npm `latest` release; `main` can be ahead of it, and every sentence traces to a line of the README or a row of the Assurance Matrix.

```text
What Sanctuary is: the wall under the agent, imposed by the operating system under a policy you sign, and it does not depend on the agent's cooperation. The keys never leave hardware you control. What the agent did is written to a hash-chained record you can read.
What it is not: no Assurance Matrix row claims a filesystem or process sandbox for the agent; that is what your harness's own sandbox provides. The record is not an audited per-rule, per-flow trail. Windows enforcement is roadmapped; nothing enforces on Windows today. Linux enforcement is proven on Ubuntu 24.04 (x86-64) only; every other distribution or architecture remains unproven. Linux enforcement ships as the separate Castle Wall Linux 0.1.0-1 package (a GitHub pre-release), not in the npm package.
Platforms and runtime: Node.js >= 22.0.0 and npm >= 10.0.0. macOS: proven. Linux: proven on Ubuntu 24.04 (x86-64) only. Windows: roadmapped.
Install:   npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server protect --claude-code --no-open --no-dashboard
Verify:    npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server doctor --json
Uninstall: npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server uninstall
Evidence: every capability claim traces to a row in ASSURANCE_MATRIX.md, and a row reads proven only when a captured drill on the platform that matters says so. Drill records are under docs/audit/.
```

## Quickstart

Copied verbatim from README.md. Three commands, in order: install, verify, uninstall. Each exists on the v1.8.4 tag that `npx` resolves to, and none of them prompts when stdin is not a terminal.

```bash
npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server protect --claude-code --no-open --no-dashboard
npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server doctor --json
npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server uninstall
```

`-y` skips npm's install prompt; without it npx asks before fetching the package in a terminal. `--no-dashboard` skips the per-call dashboard, which otherwise serves in the foreground until you stop it; wrap still persists the agent record so a separately-running `sanctuary dashboard` (or a later wrap) sees the harness; start it later with `sanctuary dashboard`.

## Bounds

Condensed from the README's "What is proven, and what is not" table. Every capability claim traces to a row in the Assurance Matrix, and a row reads proven only when a captured drill on the platform that matters says so; a green test suite is not a claim. The wall: macOS proven, as a signed operator policy with a clean per-uid allow/deny demonstration that survives attended reboot cycles, not an audited per-rule, per-flow trail. Linux: proven on Ubuntu 24.04 (x86-64) only; a fresh install of the shipped package enforces a signed operator policy per user account: blocked destinations stay blocked and allowed ones connect, through five reboots, on three fresh servers, with the evidence checked by two independent reviewers. Fault-injection witnesses, a real-agent harness, and every other distribution or architecture remain unproven. Windows: roadmapped. Custody (keys and state under your passphrase, on your hardware) and the gate (policy frozen at startup, three approval tiers) are proven. The record (hash-chained audit) and exit (keys, state, memory and reputation leave with you) are partial; the open defect ids are in the matrix.

Current stable release: v1.8.4 on the npm latest channel. Requirements: Node.js >= 22.0.0 and npm >= 10.0.0.

## Install and verify

- [Install](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#quickstart): `npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server protect --claude-code --no-open --no-dashboard`, or substitute `--openclaw`, `--hermes`, `--cursor`, `--cline`, `--mastra` (fixture-tested only; no live Mastra-agent drill recorded), or `--wrap <path-to-config>` for `--claude-code`. Protect backs up the harness config to `~/.sanctuary/backup/`, rewrites its MCP server entries to point at Sanctuary (the harness's own built-in tools are not MCP calls and are not touched; the rewrite is tested on representative harness paths and is not proven for every harness version: Assurance Matrix, Agent wrapping), and, without `--no-dashboard`, starts the Sovereignty Dashboard on `http://localhost:3501` (or the next free port, trying up to twenty ports from 3501). After `npm install -g @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server`, the `sanctuary` command replaces the `npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server` prefix. The operating-system wall is a separate privileged arming step on macOS.
- [Verify](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#health-check): `npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server doctor --json` is read-only. It prints one JSON object with `storage_path`, `package_version`, and a `checks` array whose entries carry `name`, `status` (`OK`, `WARN`, or `FAIL`), `message`, and `hint`. Healthy: exit code 0 and no check with `"status": "FAIL"`. Read `storage_path` before the checks: `doctor` pointed at the wrong `--fortress` path reports a healthy runtime and a failing fortress. Inside a wrapped harness, the `sovereignty_audit` MCP tool scores your setup 0-100 across security, isolation, and privacy; it has no CLI form.
- [Uninstall](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#quickstart): `npx -y @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server uninstall` removes Sanctuary's installed enforcement footprint and preserves the fortress state, keys, passphrase custody, recovery material, and audit log; it refuses `--remove-operator-data` by design and reports any residue that needs sudo, the Castle Wall host app, or a reboot. `sanctuary protect --unwrap` restores the original harness config from `~/.sanctuary/backup/` and removes nothing else.
- [For AI coding agents installing on behalf of an operator](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#for-ai-coding-agents-installing-sanctuary-on-behalf-of-an-operator): `sanctuary install --profile memory --harness claude-code --json`; execute only an `agent_action` argument vector, exactly once, then rerun the planner; stop on `human_action` and `blocked`; on a nonzero exit hand the operator `next_action.on_nonzero` and do not retry; treat `complete` as the only finished state. Never read the staged recovery file, run `sanctuary export-passphrase`, or capture secret output.
- [Agent-guided installation contract](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/docs/agent-guided-install.md): the observed-state planner, the secret boundary, and the cold-install acceptance criterion.
- [Verify before you trust](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#verify-before-you-trust): `npm view @sanctuary-framework/mcp-server@1.8.4 dist.attestations` prints the npm provenance attestation; the release tarball is also signed with a pinned Ed25519 key and the verifier (`scripts/verify-release-artifact.mjs`) ships in the repository.
- [Castle Wall macOS install and arm guide](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/docs/castle-wall-macos-install.md): the signed app, system extension, boot service, uninstall, and restore and recovery.
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#troubleshooting): every case is keyed to a field of `sanctuary install --json` or a check of `sanctuary doctor --json`, written for AI coding agents.

## Architecture

- [The Castle Architecture](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#the-castle-architecture): five named mechanisms, Castle Wall, Sentinels, Charter, Heralds, and Mantle, each with its bounds.
- [Sanctuary and your harness's sandbox](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#sanctuary-and-your-harnesss-sandbox): what Sanctuary adds per platform, and what the harness sandbox gives that Sanctuary never claims.
- [SANCTUARY_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/SANCTUARY_ARCHITECTURE.md): entry points, data flow, trust model, and the sovereignty properties as testable assertions.
- [Module map](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/server/src/README.md): the 64-module index of the TypeScript server, with 56 barrels.
- [Start here if you read code](https://github.com/eriknewton/sanctuary-framework/blob/main/README.md#start-here-if-you-read-code): the reading order, about an hour.
